notes:
I couldn't write the Job 4 notes this time. My first attempt to fetch the commentary pages went over the tool usage limit, and the system then blocked any further web access for this turn. No page loaded, so I have nothing sourced to report.

You asked me to use only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, because they would be unsourced.

**What I'd do next time:** I'd read these pages one or two at a time so I stay within the limit:
- **Verse-by-verse readings:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-4/, plus the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Barnes and Matthew Henry commentaries on Job 4 at biblehub.com, and preceptaustin.org.
- **Modern scholarship:** the netbible.org notes on Job 4, especially on the night vision (vv. 12–21) and the "angels charged with error" line in v. 18. Also bibleodyssey.org articles on Eliphaz and the theology of retribution.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** for example, Wesley's notes at wesley.nnu.edu, Spurgeon at spurgeon.org, and Reformed sources (Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition) on whether Eliphaz's vision really came from God and whether his "the innocent never perish" argument holds up.
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** Gregory the Great's *Moralia in Job* (newadvent.org or ccel.org) and catholic.com.
- **Popular modern teaching:** gotquestions.org and similar sites on how prosperity teaching uses Eliphaz's claim in v. 7.

If you start a new message (just "continue" will do), I'll go through these sources and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
